chunks: 5451 - And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Mūsā ibn Bakr, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
“When ten years have passed over the boy, then whatever he does with his wealth—whether he frees a slave, gives charity, or makes a bequest within a known limit and in a rightful matter—is valid.”

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he makes a bequest or will
key_terms.الْغُلَامِ: a boy, referring here to the minor whose legal capacity is being discussed
key_terms.عَلَى حَدٍّ مَعْرُوفٍ: within a recognized or reasonable limit
key_terms.فِي مَالِهِ: with respect to his property or wealth

ai.seo_question: At what age does a boy’s bequest and charitable disposal of wealth become valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a boy who has reached ten years of age, stating that certain dispositions of his property are recognized as valid. It specifically mentions emancipation, charity, and bequest, provided they are within known limits and in a rightful matter.
